posts.title: Weekly WiFi sanity check

slides.text: Restart the router — Unplug power for a full 60 seconds, then plug back in — this clears the DHCP and thermal dropouts a quick reset can't fix, and a 2.4/5 GHz router typically takes 2–3 minutes to fully come back.

Run a speed test on your main device — Test the same room as your router first (a clean baseline), then the room you use most — download AND upload, twice each. If one room is consistently 30%+ slower, that's a signal, not a coincidence.

Forget and rejoin WiFi if it's weak — WiFi adapters can pin a stale, congested channel or a dead 5 GHz band. Forget the network, power-cycle the phone, rejoin and re-enter the password so it renegotiates a fresh connection.

posts.caption:
Weekly WiFi sanity check 📱

1. Restart the router
     ✓ Unplug power for a full 60 seconds, then plug back in — this clears the DHCP and thermal dropouts a quick reset can't fix, and a 2.4/5 GHz router typically takes 2–3 minutes to fully come back.
2. Run a speed test on your main device
     ✓ Test the same room as your router first (a clean baseline), then the room you use most — download AND upload, twice each. If one room is consistently 30%+ slower, that's a signal, not a coincidence.
3. Forget and rejoin WiFi if it's weak
     ✓ WiFi adapters can pin a stale, congested channel or a dead 5 GHz band. Forget the network, power-cycle the phone, rejoin and re-enter the password so it renegotiates a fresh connection.
